audio.t: Good evening, everyone, and welcome to the first training session for our winter science camp. I'm Professor Lin, the camp director. Over five days, about sixty fifth and sixth graders from small schools in Pingtung will join us here on campus. Each of you will lead a team of six children, so you are not just a teacher. You are also a big brother or a big sister.

Tonight I want to stress three things. First, safety comes before fun. Any activity that involves heat, chemicals, or water must be checked by a staff member before you begin. Second, never leave your team alone, not even for a quick phone call. If you need a break, ask one of the floating counselors to cover for you. Third, keep your communication with parents professional. Please use the official camp group chat, not your personal accounts.
Next week, we'll practice the actual experiments, so please read the activity handbook before you come. And don't forget to hand in your health form by Friday.

head: From: Youth Outreach Club <outreach@university.edu.tw>
To: Winter Camp Applicants
Subject: Interview Arrangements for Winter Camp Counselors
passage: Thank you for applying to be a counselor at our Winter Reading Camp, which will take place from January 20 to 24 at Guangfu Elementary School in Nantou. We received 48 applications for only 16 positions, so we have decided to hold group interviews.

Interviews will take place on December 6 and 7 in Room 312 of the Student Activity Center. Please choose a time slot through the link below by December 2. Each interview lasts about forty minutes. You will work with other applicants to plan a simple reading activity for children aged eight to ten.

Please bring your student ID. If you are unable to attend on either day, reply to this email as soon as possible, and we will try to arrange an online interview. Note that online interviews are limited and will be granted only in special circumstances.

questions.explain: 信中說收到 48 份申請但只有 16 個名額，因此舉辦團體面試，故選 D。地點未更動，A 錯；仍可視情況安排線上面試，C 錯；B 未提及。

passage: For many university students, winter break means sleeping late, catching up on dramas, or working part-time. But a growing number of students in Taiwan are choosing a different way to spend their vacation: volunteering as counselors at winter camps in rural areas. According to the university's Service Learning Office, the number of students joining such camps has nearly doubled over the past three years.

The camps usually last four to seven days and focus on subjects such as English, science, or reading. In many remote villages, schools have few teachers and limited resources, so children rarely get to take part in hands-on activities. "Our counselors bring energy and fresh ideas," said Ms. Chen, the principal of a small school in Yilan. "Some of our students still talk about the robot-building activity from last year."

The experience benefits the volunteers as well. Wang Yu-ting, a junior majoring in social work, said that leading a team of ten-year-olds taught her more about communication than any class had. "You can't just give a lecture. You have to think about how kids feel and keep them interested," she explained. Many students also say the experience helps them stand out when they apply for jobs or graduate programs.

However, organizers warn that running a camp is no vacation. Counselors must attend several training sessions, prepare lesson plans, and often sleep on classroom floors. Some camps have also been criticized for being too short to make a lasting difference. To address this, a few clubs now stay in touch with the schools all year round, mailing reading materials and holding online tutoring sessions.

questions.explain: 全文從學生寒假到偏鄉擔任營隊隊輔的人數倍增談起，並說明對孩童與志工的影響及挑戰，故選 A。B、D 未提及；C 只是文中舉例的細節。
